updates.summary: Economic and energy stress remained severe while the coercive apparatus showed no evidence of systemic fracture.
Diplomacy suffered a setback while fiscal and energy stress worsened; managed oil transit through Hormuz improved for Gulf producers without restoring Iran's own export position.

Monetary / FX.text: Warning: depreciation, liquidity growth and a large managed/free-market spread show substantial movement toward an acute FX threshold.

Fiscal.text: Warning: weak sovereign financing demand, high yields and impaired oil revenue increase financing stress; ordinary financing has not clearly failed.

Banking / payments.text: Warning: alternative payment rails and import settlement face material sanctions friction, but nationwide payment-system failure is not established.

Food / medicine.text: Warning: medicine and imported-input shortages are material; evidence does not establish generalized essential-food failure.

Energy / industrial.text: Warning: rationing and conservation are affecting work patterns and industrial/logistics activity; evidence does not yet show self-reinforcing allocation failure or failure of priority users.

Social / protest.text: Watch: economic protests have broadened but remain fragmented rather than sustained nationwide coordinated unrest.

Coercive apparatus.text: Insufficient data on pay and benefits. Available reporting shows no verified refusal, desertion or defection, but absence of evidence is not coded green.

Elite cohesion.text: Watch: policy disagreement exists, but no open institutional fracture affecting command or governance is visible.

External support.text: Watch: China and Russia cushion isolation but do not replace lost oil FX and have incentives to limit destabilizing escalation.

news.title: Tehran's initial Hormuz proposal was rejected
news.impact: Reduced the negotiated-de-escalation scenario and raised prolonged-standoff and escalation cases.

news.title: Hormuz crude shuttles and managed flows increased despite severely depressed ordinary traffic
news.impact: Reuters/Kpler reporting documented continuing Saudi and Iraqi crude movement and ship-to-ship workarounds despite very low visible commercial traffic, lowering physical-delivery risk slightly without restoring Iranian oil revenue.

news.title: Emergency demand-management measures took effect
news.impact: Remote work, public-transport incentives and fuel-conservation measures strengthened evidence of a binding domestic energy imbalance.
news.source_note: Al Jazeera reported the government set 8am–1pm office attendance from September 23 with remaining hours remote, weekly public-transport days, and temporarily free metro/BRT as fuel-saving measures.

updates.what_changed: Diplomacy deteriorated while fiscal and energy evidence worsened; managed Hormuz crude movement improved without restoring Iran's own oil-export position.
updates.stabilizer: No verified coercive-system fracture or failure of priority military/security allocations.
updates.next_threshold: Whether economic and energy stress begins impairing priority state allocations or coercive-system compensation.

conditions.hormuz: Observation: commercial traffic remains severely restricted despite managed crude movements.
conditions.energy: Inference, high confidence: binding product and power constraints are producing active demand management.
conditions.coercion: No verified systemic compensation or discipline failure

forecasts.label: Sustained major regional escalation
forecasts.event_definition: Yes if, before the horizon, sustained major interstate strikes resume for at least 72 hours or major combat materially expands to an additional state/operational theater; isolated interceptions or one-off strikes do not qualify.
forecasts.raise: Repeated major US–Iran strikes, broader Saudi–Houthi war, or failure of active mediation.
forecasts.lower: Verified ceasefire implementation, sustained Hormuz normalization, or direct negotiations producing enforceable constraints.
forecasts.original_issue_definition: 30–90 day regional scenario: wider regional escalation
forecasts.current_resolution_rule_status: Later operationalization adopted 2026-10-03; use only if consistent with the original forecast meaning. Any material ambiguity at resolution must be disclosed and sensitivity-scored rather than silently resolved.

forecasts.label: Regime-ending transition
forecasts.event_definition: Yes if the Islamic Republic's governing constitutional-institutional order is replaced or loses effective national governing authority; leadership replacement within the same order is No.
forecasts.raise: Verified elite fracture, security-force compensation failure, refusal to enforce orders, defections, or sustained coordinated nationwide unrest.
forecasts.lower: Oil/FX stabilization, declining protest coordination, durable elite cohesion, and continued reliable coercive-system compensation.
forecasts.current_resolution_rule_status: Later operationalization adopted 2026-10-03; use only if consistent with the original forecast meaning. Any material ambiguity at resolution must be disclosed and sensitivity-scored rather than silently resolved.

forecasts.label: Currency crisis
forecasts.event_definition: Yes if the parallel-market rial loses at least 25% against the US dollar over any rolling 30-day period after this forecast, excluding a one-day quote anomaly.
forecasts.raise: Renewed rapid parallel-rate depreciation, failed intervention, accelerating monetary financing or shortening price/wage intervals.
forecasts.lower: Sustained rial stabilization, narrowing official–parallel spread and slower liquidity growth.

forecasts.label: External-payments crisis
forecasts.event_definition: Yes if FX/payment scarcity causes broad emergency import/payment restrictions or documented material inability to settle essential imports through normal or established alternative channels.
forecasts.raise: Further oil/payment-channel loss, import-payment breakdown, supplier prepayment demands or broad LC/settlement failure.
forecasts.lower: Restored oil receipts/payment access, improved import settlement and durable alternative payment channels.

chains.name: FX / fiscal
chains.note: Depreciation is confirmed; intervention is under strain but not established as failed. Generalized high-frequency repricing and runaway monetization are not established.
chains.pathway_note: Diagnostic pathway, not a required causal sequence: stages may be skipped, reversed or reached through another mechanism.

chains.name: Energy / real economy
chains.note: Rationing/conservation and industrial/freight disruption are confirmed; essential-goods stress is present but not yet a generalized shortage threshold. Failure of priority allocations remains absent.
chains.pathway_note: Diagnostic pathway, not a required causal sequence: stages may be skipped, reversed or reached through another mechanism.

chains.name: Regime / coercion
chains.note: Economic protest is confirmed; movement toward coordinated national protest is being watched, while elite fracture and coercive refusal are not established.
chains.pathway_note: Diagnostic pathway, not a required causal sequence: stages may be skipped, reversed or reached through another mechanism.

haircut.note: Risk adjustment may appear through price, tenor, collateral or payment timing rather than an explicit discount.

method.label: Model estimate
method.rule: Central haircut = sum of six bounded component haircuts: physical delivery/blockade 0–25 pp; sanctions/payment channels 0–15; sovereign/counterparty 0–10; oil-price/basis 0–8; illiquidity/enforcement 0–8; political/secondary-sanctions tail 0–8. Each component is assigned from documented weekly evidence using Low/Mid/High anchors at 25/50/75% of its cap; the central estimate is the sum rounded to the nearest percentage point. The judgmental range is formed by moving each uncertain component one anchor step down/up, bounded at zero/cap. This is not an observed contract price.

houthi.definition: Strategically meaningful Houthi support is decomposed into Iranian matériel flow, Iranian technical/financial assistance, and Houthi independent/local capability. The headline support-continuity probability refers only to continued Iranian technical/financial or material support sufficient to measurably sustain advanced missile/UAV or maritime capability; local capability alone does not resolve it Yes.

absence_indicators.label: Security-force defections
absence_indicators.text: No verified consequential defections or unit-level refusal, but reporting coverage is insufficient for affirmative Normal status.

absence_indicators.label: Nationwide bazaar shutdown
absence_indicators.text: No verified nationwide coordinated bazaar closure.

absence_indicators.label: Priority military/security fuel failure
absence_indicators.text: No failure is reported, but public observation is too weak to treat absence as affirmative reassurance.

absence_indicators.label: Economy-wide high-frequency wage indexation
absence_indicators.text: No generalized high-frequency automatic wage repricing is verified, but observation coverage is insufficient for affirmative Normal status.

absence_indicators.label: Systemically important Chinese-bank cutoff
absence_indicators.text: No verified cutoff by a major Chinese bank; Chinese support remains conditional but material.

binary_political.label: Islamic Republic governing order survives 12 months

updates.regional_resolution_note: Scenario buckets are descriptive legacy partitions. Scored forecasting uses the binary sustained-major-escalation definition above; future scenario partitions must include explicit mutually exclusive resolution rules.
updates.political_resolution_note: Political outcome buckets are retained as a legacy descriptive partition. Scored forecasting uses separate binary events because institutional restructuring and external stabilization can co-occur.
updates.limitations: Iranian economic, military and political data are incomplete, delayed, sometimes contradictory and strategically manipulated. Open-source visibility is asymmetric across institutions and regions. Probabilities therefore reflect the stated public information set, not complete knowledge.

evidence.observation: US rejection of Tehran's initial Hormuz proposal was reported.
Reuters/Kpler reported continued managed Saudi/Iraqi crude movement despite severely depressed ordinary Hormuz traffic.
Government office-hour, remote-work and public-transport measures were reported as fuel-saving measures beginning September 23.

methodology_notes: Protocol v1.0 was frozen on 2026-10-03 for prospective forecasts beginning 2026-10-04. It is not retroactively applied to the 2026-09-27 forecast.
updates.revision_attribution_status: Not reconstructed retrospectively; signed contribution accounting begins prospectively under Protocol v1 on 2026-10-04.

uncertainty_rule.name: Reasonable-analyst interval
uncertainty_rule.definition: The displayed judgmental uncertainty range is the interval within which the assessor judges that roughly 80% of independent, well-informed analysts using the same public information, event definition and horizon would place their point probability. It measures model/analyst disagreement, not sampling error, a Bayesian credible interval, or the probability that the true probability lies in the interval.
uncertainty_rule.elicitation: Set the point forecast first. Then estimate the 10th and 90th percentiles of the distribution of reasonable analysts' point forecasts without changing the point forecast to center the range.

prospective_scoring_rule: A forecast is eligible for scoring only if scored=true and its created_date is on or before its forecast publication date. Retrospective decompositions are preserved for methodological transparency but excluded from Brier scores and calibration.

protocol.change_policy: Protocol v1 is frozen for prospective use. Substantive changes require a new numbered protocol version, an effective date, a change log, and no retroactive application to already-issued forecasts.
protocol.timestamp_policy: Evidence collection closes before forecast elicitation. Each update records evidence_cutoff as the actual last evidence timestamp used and publication_time as the actual commit/publication timestamp. Material information first available after evidence_cutoff is excluded from that forecast and may enter only the next forecast or an explicitly labeled interim update.

core_scored_set.resolution: Yes if sustained major interstate strikes occur for at least 72 consecutive hours, or major combat materially expands to an additional sovereign state/operational theater. One-off strikes, interceptions, isolated proxy attacks, or rhetoric alone are No unless they initiate the qualifying sustained episode.

Yes if the Islamic Republic's governing constitutional-institutional order is replaced or loses effective national governing authority. Leadership succession, cabinet change, or factional turnover within the same governing order is No.

Yes if the parallel-market rial depreciates at least 25% against the US dollar over any rolling 30-calendar-day window, using the designated consistent parallel-rate series and excluding a single-day quote anomaly that reverses within 48 hours.
core_scored_set.threshold_note: The 25%/30-day threshold is a monitoring convention chosen ex ante for Protocol v1 for scoreability and sensitivity to acute depreciation; it is not claimed to be a universal economic definition. Sensitivity at 20% and 30% will be reported when resolving.

core_scored_set.resolution: Yes if at least two essential-import categories (food/grain, medicine/medical inputs, or critical energy/industrial inputs) show corroborated settlement disruption lasting at least 14 days AND the government imposes broad emergency FX/import/payment restrictions or suppliers materially shift to prepayment/cash because established settlement channels are failing. Evidence must come from at least two independent source streams.

protocol.noncore_policy: Other probabilities may be published as diagnostic estimates but are not part of the permanent core scored set unless added prospectively in a later protocol version.

uncertainty_rule.name: Reasonable-analyst interval
uncertainty_rule.definition: The displayed judgmental uncertainty range is the interval within which the assessor judges that roughly 80% of independent, well-informed analysts using the same public information, event definition and horizon would place their point probability. It measures model/analyst disagreement, not sampling error, a Bayesian credible interval, or the probability that the true probability lies in the interval.
uncertainty_rule.elicitation: Set the point forecast first. Then estimate the 10th and 90th percentiles of the distribution of reasonable analysts' point forecasts without changing the point forecast to center the range.

evidence_reliability.High: Primary/direct evidence or multiple independent highly credible sources; direct and current; no material contradiction.
evidence_reliability.Medium-high: Credible and substantially direct evidence with at least one corroborating stream, or exceptionally strong single-source evidence.
evidence_reliability.Medium: Credible but indirect, incompletely corroborated, or subject to meaningful measurement/reporting uncertainty.
evidence_reliability.Low: Single-source, materially indirect, stale, contested, or weakly observable evidence. Low evidence cannot by itself trigger Critical.

Monetary / FX.green: Stable parallel rate/spread and functioning intervention/payment access on affirmative evidence.
Monetary / FX.yellow: Persistent depreciation/spread widening or rising dollarization without intervention failure.
Monetary / FX.orange: Multiple signals: accelerating depreciation plus ineffective intervention/payment strain or shortening quote validity.
Monetary / FX.red: Self-reinforcing substitution/repricing dynamics or qualifying currency crisis already operating.

Fiscal.green: Routine financing clears without extraordinary coercion/monetization.
Fiscal.yellow: Rising yields, arrears pressure or weaker auctions.
Fiscal.orange: Repeated weak/failed financing plus forced lending, fund drawdown or material monetization.
Fiscal.red: Routine financing failure with accelerating monetization/arrears threatening priority obligations.

Banking / payments.yellow: Localized delays, higher prepayment or channel friction.
Banking / payments.orange: Multiple sectors/channels show persistent settlement failure or material deposit/dollarization stress.
Banking / payments.red: Broad payment impairment or bank/liquidity dysfunction disrupting essential commerce.

Food / medicine.orange: Multiple essential categories materially disrupted across regions.
Food / medicine.red: Generalized essential-goods failure with rationing/queues and logistics/payment feedback.

Energy / industrial.green: Normal reserve margins/supply with no emergency curtailment.
Energy / industrial.yellow: Conservation appeals, localized curtailment or seasonal stress.
Energy / industrial.orange: Rationing/load shedding materially disrupts industry, freight or work patterns.
Energy / industrial.red: Priority allocations fail or energy disruption becomes self-reinforcing across essential logistics/production.

Social / protest.green: Affirmative low protest activity and normal commerce.
Social / protest.orange: Sustained multi-city coordination, major sectoral convergence or nationwide commercial disruption.
Social / protest.red: Nationwide sustained unrest materially impairing governance or coercive control.

Coercive apparatus.green: Affirmative evidence timely compensation, attendance and command compliance.
Coercive apparatus.yellow: Verified localized pay/benefit or morale problems.
Coercive apparatus.orange: Repeated arrears/absenteeism/refusal across units or services.
Coercive apparatus.red: Material command noncompliance, unit-level refusal, defections or inability to protect priority state functions.

Elite cohesion.yellow: Public blame, unusual clerical/business criticism or personnel churn.
Elite cohesion.orange: Open institutional conflict affecting policy implementation or command.
Elite cohesion.red: Competing centers of authority or elite fracture impairing national command.

External support.yellow: Support continues but with rising discounts/frictions.
External support.orange: Major channels materially impaired or partners visibly reduce exposure.
External support.red: External lifelines fail across multiple critical channels with no adequate substitute.

haircut_protocol.dependence_rule: Component contributions are not simply interpreted as independent risks. Protocol v1 applies a 20% overlap deduction to the combined delivery + sanctions/payment + political-tail subtotal above 20 percentage points, rounded to the nearest point, to reduce double counting of a common geopolitical shock.

Physical delivery/blockade.low: Routine evasion/managed delivery with limited disruption
Physical delivery/blockade.mid: Persistent disruption/workarounds and meaningful delivery uncertainty
Physical delivery/blockade.high: Severe route denial/blockade or repeated delivery failure

Sovereign/counterparty.high: Repeated nonperformance or acute sovereign stress

haircut_protocol.sensitivity: Alongside the v1 20% overlap convention, report sensitivity using 0%, 20%, and 40% overlap deductions. The 20% case remains the Protocol v1 headline; sensitivity cases are diagnostic and do not change the frozen rule.
haircut_protocol.overlap_status: The 20% overlap factor is an explicit Protocol v1 convention, not an empirically estimated correlation parameter. It is a candidate for empirical revision only in a future protocol version.

houthi_protocol.headline_resolution: Yes only if Iranian matériel or Iranian technical/financial support remains sufficient to measurably sustain advanced Houthi missile/UAV or maritime capability. Houthi independent/local capability alone cannot resolve Iranian-support continuity Yes.
houthi_protocol.elicitation: Assess matériel and technical/financial support separately from local capability; headline probability is a judgment conditioned on at least one Iranian-support channel remaining strategically meaningful.

protocol.calibration_policy: Report Brier scores for all resolved core forecasts and separately by event family and comparable horizon only when sample size is adequate; never imply meaningful calibration from very small cells.
protocol.evidence_balance_policy: For each core forecast, preserve material evidence that raises, lowers, or is genuinely ambiguous/neutral. A zero probability revision may be labeled 'offsetting evidence' when meaningful opposing evidence changed but net probability did not.

resolution_policy.authority: Resolve from the pre-specified event rule using the archived public evidence record. Ambiguous cases require a written resolution note citing the decisive evidence and rule clause.
resolution_policy.indeterminate: If reliable public evidence is insufficient to determine Yes or No by the resolution review date, code outcome='indeterminate'. Indeterminate forecasts are excluded from Brier/calibration scoring; the exclusion and reason remain public. Never choose a resolution based on which result improves the score.
resolution_policy.review_timing: Perform resolution review promptly after the forecast deadline; later evidence may establish what happened before the deadline only if it directly documents the pre-deadline state.

protocol.serial_dependence_caveat: Weekly forecasts with overlapping horizons are strongly serially dependent. Per-forecast Brier scores may be reported, but counts of overlapping forecasts must not be interpreted as independent sample size; calibration uncertainty and comparative claims must account for clustering/overlap.
protocol.display_clarification: Warning colors describe the current state of a diagnostic failure pathway. Forecast probabilities describe the chance of a defined future event by a stated deadline. A severe current warning and a lower future-event probability, or vice versa, are not inherently inconsistent.

evidence_impact_scale.minor: Credible evidence that modestly updates one input but does not alter the central mechanism or threshold state.
evidence_impact_scale.moderate: Corroborated evidence that materially changes a key driver, threshold state, or one core forecast's assessment.
evidence_impact_scale.major: High-quality evidence of a structural break, threshold crossing, major military/political/economic event, or failure/restoration of a critical mechanism.

protocol.revision_attribution_rule: At forecast time, record approximate signed percentage-point contributions for material new evidence/reassessment sufficient to reconcile the prior point forecast to the new point forecast. These are an audit decomposition of judgment, not causal estimates or a statistical model. If effects offset, label offsetting evidence.

id_policy.forecast_id: core event id + '_' + forecast date YYYYMMDD; immutable once issued.
id_policy.evidence_id: Persistent event/source identifier. Reuse the same evidence_id when evidence is carried forward; mark evidence_status='new' or 'carried_forward' rather than creating a duplicate observation.

protocol.uncertainty_display: Display the reasonable-analyst interval less prominently than the point forecast and evidence confidence until external forecaster dispersion can be compared with it.

protocol_v1_1_candidate_register: Empirically estimate dependence/overlap in the Iran–China oil-credit haircut rather than using the v1 20% convention.
Replace qualitative haircut Low/Mid/High anchors with more observable quantitative thresholds where reliable data permit.
Validate reasonable-analyst uncertainty intervals against actual external-forecaster dispersion when a comparable sample becomes available.
Evaluate whether the 90-day escalation rule needs a prospectively defined high-severity alternative to the 72-hour criterion.
Evaluate resolution-authority procedures for fragmented or contested national control using experience from resolved forecasts.
